paper_metadata.title: A Comparison between Ultra-high-strength and Conventional High-strength Fastener Steels: Mechanical Properties at Elevated Temperature and Microstructural Mechanisms

evidence.quote: A comparison is made between the mechanical properties of the ultra-high-strength steel KNDS4 of fastener grade 14.9 and of conventional, high-strength steels 34Cr4 of fastener grade 12.9 and 33B2 of grade 10.9.

There are several precipitate types which can generate precipitation strengthening in KNDS4_1350: M7C3 alloy carbides which form during quenching, Ti4C2S2 which can form during the austenitization and possibly small iron carbides from auto-tempering.

ThermoCalc shows that Ti4C2S2 is stable in austenite at temperatures higher than 1 070°C. It is therefore possible that Ti4C2S2 nucleates as small precipitates during austenitization of KNDS4_1350. The equilibrium volume fraction of Ti4C2S2 in KNDS4_1350 is 3.77·10–4 at 1 350°C. This volume fraction of precipitates of size 0.62 nm can generate a hardness increase of 25 HV.
